channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Breaking: New Zealand’s CPI inflation climbs to 4.1% YoY in Q2, vs 4.0% expected
item.description: New Zealand’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 4.1% YoY in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026, compared with the 3.1% increase seen in the first quarter, according to the latest data published by Statistics New Zealand on Tuesday. The market consensus was for a growth of 4.0% in the reported period.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Uptrend pauses, bulls eye 219 breakout
item.description: The Pound Sterling registers losses against the Japanese Yen for the third consecutive trading day, doon 0.15% as traders digest the first speech of new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is naming the first members of his cabinet. The GBP/JPY trades at 218.13 after reaching a daily high of 218.84.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Rangebound trade guided by fix against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong see USD/CNH staying broadly rangebound as the People's Bank of China (PBoC) fixing continues to anchor moves. Softer US inflation has recently weighed on the Dollar while firmer fixings allowed some gradual Renminbi (CNH) strength.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Reclaims 0.8100 as market structure is bullish
item.description: The Swiss Franc loses ground against the Greenback in a trading session marked by CHF weakness amid improving risk appetite. At the time of writing, the USD/CHF trades at 0.8101, up 0.32%.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Growth supports range against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao and Moses Lim report that Malaysia’s stronger-than-expected Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth and subdued inflation support an unchanged policy rate of 2.75%. USD/MYR has remained within a 4.05–4.10 range, recently edging higher alongside crude oil prices.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD is stuck in a tight range after recent sideways trading, with intraday action expected between 1.2900 and 1.2930. On a 1–3 week horizon, the bank still sees downside risks if 1.2860 breaks, while 1.2930 remains strong resistance.

item.title: Mexican Peso gains as risk appetite boosts Peso, weighs on USD
item.description: The Mexican Peso gains some ground versus the Greenback on Monday, up by 0.66% as risk appetite improves despite escalating tensions in the Middle East. At the time of writing, the USD/MXN trades at 17.43 after hitting a daily high of 17.55

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rises as Gulf tensions lift, Oil and Canadian inflation cool
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) rises around 0.2% toward 101.00 as higher United States (US) Treasury yields and escalating tensions in the Middle East support the Greenback.

item.title: Crude Oil spends Monday selling the war, then buys the revenge post
item.description: Crude Oil compressed its entire 2026 personality into a single Monday tape.

item.title: Asia FX: Oil rebound pressures INR and THB – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that higher Oil prices and persistent inflation risks are weighing on Asian currencies, with the Indian Rupee (INR) and Thai Baht (THB) underperforming against the US Dollar.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics support crude and cracks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem highlight that Brent has surged as US-Iran tensions, Trump’s rhetoric and Houthi blockade threats lift risk premia. Crack spreads in Asia and US have outperformed as refined products stay tighter than crude.

item.title: China: Chinese AI models challenge US-led economics – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists analyses China’s AI (Artificial intelligence) ecosystem, noting that Chinese models are rapidly catching up in capability while being priced near mid-tier US systems.

item.title: Gold edges lower as Middle East conflict boosts the US Dollar
item.description: Gold price edges down some 0.19% on Monday as hostilities between the US and Iran extended, following a short-lived truce that began after both countries agreed to a ceasefire, which was broken nine days ago. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades at $4,011.

item.title: Copper: Speculators rebuild longs on tight supply – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategy team highlights that, after a five‑week reduction in Copper longs, speculators have resumed adding net length, supported by firm Chinese premiums, low arrivals and inventory draws on the LME and SHFE.

item.title: Canadian Dollar falls as softer Canadian inflation weighs on the Loonie
item.description: USD/CAD trades higher near the 1.4060 area on Monday, recovering from below 1.4000 as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) weakens following softer-than-expected domestic inflation data. The US Dollar Index (DXY) also rises around 0.2% near 101.00, providing additional support to the pair.

item.title: United States Dollar Index advances as Middle East tensions drive demand
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) edges higher on Monday as heightened tensions in the Middle East drive demand for the safe-haven Greenback.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD attempts to stabilize above $55.00
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades on the front foot on Monday as buyers defend the $55.00 mark after the metal briefly slipped below it on Friday, touching its lowest level since December 2025. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $56.85, up nearly 1.50% on the day.

item.title: Trump declares retaliation against Iran automatic in Truth Social post
item.description: Donald Trump opened the week on Truth Social with a promise that every American soldier killed by Iran will be repaid many times over, a directive he says has been passed to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Daniel Caine, and every leader in the military.

item.title: British Pound slips as Burnham fiscal pledge fails to lift Sterling
item.description: The Pound Sterling reverses course and turns negative on the day as Andy Burnham is named the new Prime Minister and reassures that he will stick to the fiscal rules set by the former Chancellor, Rachel Reeves, who just resigned. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3425, after hitting a daily high of 1.3481.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average sits out a rally priced for a peace nobody has scheduled
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near the 52,000 handle on Monday, down roughly 100 points, while the S&P 500 adds 0.4% and the NASDAQ Composite climbs 0.9%, with all three coming off a losing week.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds as PBOC stands firm
item.description: AUD/USD trades around the 0.7000 area on Monday, holding near recent highs after recovering from last week’s decline.

item.title: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves resigns as Andy Burnham reshuffles cabinet
item.description: The United Kingdom entered a new period of political uncertainty after Rachel Reeves stepped down as Chancellor of the Exchequer as part of the first cabinet reshuffle led by newly appointed Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics support crude and cracks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem highlight that Brent has surged as US-Iran tensions, Trump’s rhetoric and Houthi blockade threats lift risk premia. Crack spreads in Asia and US have outperformed as refined products stay tighter than crude.

item.title: Euro loses momentum as US Dollar recovers from intraday lows
item.description: EUR/USD edges lower on Monday, reversing earlier gains as markets swing between risk-on and risk-off sentiment. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1408, easing from an intraday high of 1.1449.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as renewed Middle East tensions lift US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 162.55 on Monday at the time of writing, up 0.10% on the day. After an initial pullback in the US Dollar (USD), the pair regains momentum as geopolitical concerns return to the forefront and support the Greenback.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Rate divergence weighs CAD against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that softer Canadian Consumer Price Index (CPI) is lifting USD/CAD as rate divergence remains a key driver. They argue broad US Dollar (USD) strength should limit USD/CAD downside below 1.40 and see higher Oil prices as CAD-supportive on crosses but not versus USD.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry supports resilience against US Dollar - BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu sees Latin American currencies underpinned by strong balance-of-payments positions and attractive carry, even as global equity nerves rise.

item.title: Gold swings around $4,000 as conflicting Middle East headlines drive markets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades in a volatile range on Monday as markets react to conflicting headlines from the Middle East. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,010, little changed on the day after climbing to an intra-day high of $4,040.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Carry and growth support potential rebound – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists argue AUD/USD has room to rise into 2027, supported by Australia’s relatively high cash and government bond yields, which make the Australian Dollar attractive on a carry basis within G10 FX.

item.title: Gold: Fed risks and Dollar strength cap upside – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategists, led by Bart Melek, note that Gold investors have sharply reduced long exposure as higher Oil prices from the US‑Iran conflict threaten recent disinflation progress.
